newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mobile phones push Mannesmann 9-mth sales.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phones push Mannesmann 9-mth sales.

text.p: German engineering group Mannesmann AG on Tuesday announced improved nine-month sales and flat orders, and the company said it expected a slight improvement in its operating level result for the full year.
Sales rose to 23.9 billion marks ($15.9 billion) from 22.6 billion. Order intake was unchanged at 27 billion marks, with changes in group consolidation resulting in a one percent drop in the figure.

Mannesmann gave no profit figure, but said the "favourable development of group earnings" was mainly attributable to its telecommunications and automotive operations. Its traditional engineering and tubes businesses posted weaker results.
Mannesmann Mobilfunk's D2 German mobile telephone network boosted earnings, but start-up losses in its fixed-line businesses increased, according to a statement.

Mobile phone sales jumped to three billion marks from 1.9 billion, with the number of D2 subscribers increasing to 2.1 million at the end of September. Customer growth outstripped the first nine months of 1995 by 63 percent.
Mannesmann's workforce was reduced by 3,000 to 120,000 as a result of portfolio optimisation measures, the company said.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.502 German Marks)
